topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the core learning objectives of the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, intrinsic mutations, and environmental risk factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamentals of cancer development by evaluating intrinsic genetic mutations and random processes alongside environmental exposures and global epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens and cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological infectious agents contribute to tumorigenesis, illustrated by the specific etiology and mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how chemical and physical agents induce DNA damage directly or through metabolic activation and oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, microenvironmental factors, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic drivers of carcinogenesis, including tumor promotion, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental or tissue-specific host susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and evaluating exposure risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to establish carcinogenicity and weigh human exposure risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the concluding remarks and final summary of the main themes discussed throughout the lecture.
